mainTopic: Extra payments of the אונס, the hundred-סלע fine of the מוציא שם רע, the severity of לשון הרע learned from the מרגלים, and the ten tests in the desert.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a question: how do we know that an אונס pays בושת and פגם on top of the fixed fifty-shekel קנס? רב זירא's argument from fairness is rejected by אביי, because the תורה also sets a flat thirty for any עבד. אביי then brings a source from 'תחת אשר ענה', and רבא brings one from 'השוכב עמה'. Next, a new משנה teaches that the מוציא שם רע always pays a fixed hundred סלע. From this the משנה learns that harming with speech is worse than harming with an act, and it supports the point from the מרגלים in the desert. The גמרא defends both proofs from challenges using פסוקים. It then brings רבי אלעזר בן פרטא's קל וחומר: if slandering the land was punished so harshly, slandering a person is much worse. Finally, a ברייתא of רבי יהודה lists the ten times our ancestors tested הקדוש ברוך הוא, and the גמרא begins explaining each one. That list includes the story of the sea giving up the drowned מצרים, and the explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A logical argument: the same fifty for a damaged and an undamaged girl cannot be fair
steps.stepSummary: רב זירא continues his logical argument. If two men attacked a girl, one in an unnatural way and one in the natural way, people would complain if each paid the same fifty. So the fifty must be a fixed fine, with the real damage paid separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: If two men forced themselves on her, one in an unnatural way and one in the natural way, people would say: the one who attacked a damaged girl pays fifty, and the one who attacked a whole girl also pays fifty?
steps.whatsHappening: רב זירא is finishing his proof, from common sense, that an אונס pays בושת and פגם beyond the fifty. He shows that a fixed fifty alone would give an unfair result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first attacker leaves her בתולים whole, so the second one is the one who pays the קנס. But by then she is already damaged, and the second still pays the full fifty, the same as an attacker of a fully whole girl. Since that seems unfair, רב זירא concludes that the fifty is a flat fine, and the actual damage (בושת and פגם) is paid on top, according to each case.

keyTerms.meaning: Not in the natural way (does not take away her בתולים)
In the natural way
A girl who is already damaged or lowered in value
A whole, undamaged girl
Had relations with

steps.confusionAlert: This line is a continuation of רב זירא's argument, which started before this section. It is not a new speaker.

phrases.english: If two men came upon her,
one in an unnatural way and one in the natural way,
people will say: one who had a damaged girl pays fifty,
and one who had a whole girl pays fifty?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילּוּ בָּאוּ עָלֶיהָ שְׁנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב זירא's logical argument, which began before this section.
steps.raayaObject: That an אונס pays בושת and פגם in addition to the fifty
steps.raayaSupportSource: Logic: equal payment for unequal damage would look unfair to people
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fifty is a fixed קנס, and the real damage is paid separately.

steps.title: אביי rejects the logic: the תורה also fixes thirty for any slave
steps.stepSummary: אביי points out that by the same reasoning people would complain that a healthy עבד and a sick עבד are both worth thirty when killed by an ox. The תורה does fix thirty for every עבד, so 'people will complain' is no proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If so, about a slave too people will say: a healthy slave is thirty, and a slave covered with boils is thirty!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי knocks down רב זירא's logical argument by showing that the same complaint would apply to a case where we know the תורה really does give one fixed amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When an ox kills an עבד, the owner pays thirty שקלים no matter what the עבד was worth. If the תורה can set one flat amount there, even though it seems unequal, it could also set a flat fifty for an אונס. So common sense alone cannot prove that בושת and פגם are added.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if your reasoning is right)
A healthy slave
Covered with boils, a sick and low-value person
Thirty (שקלים), the fixed payment for an עבד killed by an ox

phrases.english: אביי said to him: If so,
regarding a slave too, people will say:
phrases.notes: He means an עבד killed by an ox, where the owner pays thirty (שמות 21:32).

phrases.english: a healthy slave is thirty,
and a slave covered with boils is thirty!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: אִי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the logical proof given in Step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the logic-based proof. It does not reject the ruling itself, since בושת and פגם are still paid.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The 'people will complain' argument proves too much: the תורה clearly sets a flat thirty for any עבד despite the unequal values.

steps.title: אביי's own source: 'because he tormented her'
steps.stepSummary: אביי learns from the words 'תחת אשר ענה' that the fifty pays only for the torment. That implies בושת and פגם are paid in addition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: The פסוק says 'because he tormented her.' From this we learn that there is also בושת and פגם.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the logical proof, אביי gives a source from the פסוק itself for why בושת and פגם are paid beyond the fifty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק explains that the fifty is given 'because he tormented her.' Since the fifty is tied to the torment itself, the other losses, her humiliation and her drop in value, are not included in it. They must be paid separately.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (dropping the earlier answer for a new one)
Because he tormented her (דברים 22:29)
It can be inferred, by implication
Payment for humiliation
Payment for loss of value

phrases.english: Rather, אביי said,
the verse says: 'because he tormented her,'
which implies that there is also humiliation and loss of value.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected logical proof with a source from the פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that an אונס pays בושת and פגם beyond the fifty
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'תחת אשר ענה' shows that the fifty is for the torment only, so בושת and פגם are separate.

steps.title: רבא's different source: the fifty is for the pleasure of the act
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns from 'the man who lay with her' that the fifty pays for the pleasure of lying with her. So other payments must exist, namely בושת and פגם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The פסוק says 'the man who lay with her shall give,' meaning the pleasure of lying with her is fifty. This implies there is something else to pay. And what is it? בושת and פגם.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second, different source from the same פסוק for the same rule: בושת and פגם are paid on top of the fifty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי focused on the words 'because he tormented her.' רבא focuses on 'the man who lay with her,' and reads the fifty as payment for the pleasure of the act. Since the fifty covers only that, the girl's humiliation and loss of value must be paid in addition.

keyTerms.meaning: The pleasure of lying with her
Another matter, a separate payment
And what is it?

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees that an אונס pays בושת and פגם beyond the fifty-shekel קנס. רב זירא's logical proof was rejected because of the flat thirty for an עבד. אביי learns the rule from 'תחת אשר ענה', and רבא learns it from 'השוכב עמה' (the fifty is for the pleasure of the act).

phrases.english: רבא said: because the verse says:
'Then the man who lay with her shall give,' and so on,
the pleasure of lying with her is fifty,
which implies that there is another matter,
and what is it? Humiliation and loss of value.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר, דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different source from the same פסוק, in place of אביי's.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that an אונס pays בושת and פגם beyond the fifty
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'השוכב עמה' shows that the fifty is for the pleasure of the act, so בושת and פגם are separate payments.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: בושת and פגם are paid beyond the fifty. אביי and רבא only disagree about which words of the פסוק teach it.

steps.title: The defamer pays one hundred no matter who the girl is
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that the מוציא שם רע always pays a fixed hundred סלע, whatever the girl's family status.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: With the man who spreads a bad name about his wife, there are leniencies and stringencies. How so? Whether he defamed the most important girl in the כהונה or the simplest girl in ישראל, he pays one hundred סלע.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה states a new rule: the מוציא שם רע pays one fixed amount, a hundred סלע, for every girl.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the fine is fixed, it can work out lenient (a very important girl gets no more) or strict (a simple girl gets the full hundred). The girl's family status does not change the amount.

keyTerms.meaning: One who spreads a false bad name, here a husband who falsely claims his bride was not a virgin
For leniency and for strictness
The most prominent girl in the priestly families
A silver coin; the תורה's shekel

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
With regard to one who spreads a bad name,
there are leniencies and stringencies. How so?
Both one who spread a bad name
about the most prominent girl in the priesthood,
and about the lowliest girl in Israel,
gives one hundred sela.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמוֹצִיא שֵׁם רַע לְהָקֵל וּלְהַחֲמִיר, כֵּיצַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the fifty-סלע fine of the אונס and מפתה to the hundred-סלע fine of the מוציא שם רע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מוציא שם רע pays a fixed one hundred סלע, regardless of the girl's status.

steps.title: Speaking evil is worse than doing an act, proven from the desert
steps.stepSummary: From the double fine, the משנה concludes that harming with speech is more severe than harming with an act, and supports this from the מרגלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It turns out that one who speaks with his mouth is treated more harshly than one who does an act. For we find that the decree against our ancestors in the desert was sealed only because of לשון הרע, as it says: "They tested Me these ten times."
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה draws a lesson from the numbers: the man who only spoke pays a hundred, while the men who acted pay fifty, so speech is treated as worse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אונס and מפתה actually did something to the girl, yet pay only fifty. The מוציא שם רע only talked, yet pays a hundred. The משנה backs this up with the desert: there were ten sins, but only the לשון הרע of the מרגלים sealed the decree.

keyTerms.meaning: It turns out; it comes out that
More severe, treated more harshly
A decree of punishment
Evil speech about others

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה is a classic source for how seriously חז"ל treat לשון הרע.

phrases.english: It turns out that one who speaks with his mouth
is more severe than one who does an act,
for so we have found
that the decree was not sealed
upon our ancestors in the desert
except because of evil speech,
phrases.notes: This means the bad report the מרגלים gave about ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: as it is said:
"And they tested Me these ten times, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: נִמְצָא הָאוֹמֵר בְּפִיו חָמוּר מִן הָעוֹשֶׂה מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general lesson from the fine set in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Harming with speech is more severe than harming with an act, as shown by the double fine and by the מרגלים.

steps.title: Maybe the bigger fine is because he could get her killed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the משנה knows the higher fine is for the speech; maybe it is because his claim could lead to her death.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: How do you know this? Maybe he pays more because his claim could cause her death, as it is written: "But if the thing was true... then they shall bring out the girl..."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's lesson. It suggests a different reason for the hundred-סלע fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If his claim were true, she would be stoned. So maybe the extra fine is because he nearly caused her death, which is much worse than ordinary damage. If so, the fine says nothing about speech being worse than action.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know? How is this proven?
Perhaps, maybe
He causes her death

phrases.english: GEMARA:
From where do we know this?
Perhaps it is because
he could cause her death,
as it is written:
"But if the thing was true, etc.
then they shall bring out the girl, etc."!
phrases.notes: דברים 22:20-21. The פסוק goes on to say she would be stoned.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי? דִּלְמָא מִשּׁוּם דְּקָא גָרֵים לַהּ קְטָלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference made in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's proof that speech is worse than action from the hundred-סלע fine.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The higher fine could be explained by the danger of death his claim created, not by the fact that it was speech.

steps.title: The פסוק says the fine is for the bad name itself
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the פסוק ties the fine directly to the bad name he spread, not to the danger of death.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The פסוק says "because he spread a bad name", meaning he pays for the bad name that he spread.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends the משנה by pointing to the words of the פסוק that explain why the man pays.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה itself gives the reason for the fine: "because he spread a bad name." It does not say "because he endangered her life." So the fine really is for the words, and the משנה's lesson stands.

keyTerms.meaning: For the bad name that he spread

steps.whatToRemember: The מוציא שם רע pays a hundred because of his words, as the פסוק says. That is why speech is treated as worse than action.

phrases.english: Rava said: The verse says:
"because he spread a bad name,"
he pays for the bad name that he spread.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, אָמַר קְרָא: כִּי הוֹצִיא שֵׁם רָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the wording of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fine might be because his claim could lead to her execution.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק says the fine is for the bad name itself, so it is a penalty for speech.

steps.title: Maybe the spies' sin was just the last straw
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's claim that the sentence was sealed because of the מרגלים, and asks: maybe it was sealed only because their total sins finally added up, as רב המנונא teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And so we found that the sentence was sealed only because of לשון הרע.' How do we know? Maybe their measure of sin was simply not full until then. רב המנונא said: הקדוש ברוך הוא does not punish a person until his measure is full, as the פסוק says, 'When his measure is full, he will be in trouble.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line in the משנה and challenges its proof. Maybe the מרגלים' sin was not the reason for the punishment, just the last sin in a long list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה wanted to show that bad speech is especially severe, because only the spies' report sealed the sentence. But according to רב המנונא, punishment comes once the total of sins is full. So the spies' sin might be the final drop, not a special sin, and the proof would fall away.

keyTerms.meaning: A final sentence or decree of punishment
Was sealed, made final
A measure; here, the full amount of sins that brings punishment
Collects payment, meaning punishes
Perhaps, maybe

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the מרגלים did nothing wrong. It only questions whether their sin was the special cause of the sealed sentence, or just the final one.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן מָצִינוּ שֶׁלֹּא נִתְחַתֵּם גְּזַר דִּין וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: And so we found that the sentence was sealed only, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה. The full line ends: only because of לשון הרע, the bad report of the מרגלים.

phrases.aramaic: מִמַּאי? דִּלְמָא דְּאַכַּתִּי לָא מְלָא סְאָתָן,
phrases.english: From where do we know this? Perhaps their measure was not yet full until then,
as Rav Hamnuna says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא נִפְרָע מִן הָאָדָם
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, does not punish a person
until his measure is filled,
as it is said: "When his measure is full, he will be in trouble."

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי דִּלְמָא דְּאַכַּתִּי לָא מְלָא סְאָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the second half of the משנה's proof (the מרגלים) and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's claim that the sentence in the desert was sealed specifically because of the מרגלים' לשון הרע.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Punishment comes when the total of sins is full (רב המנונא), so the spies' sin may only have been the final one, not a uniquely severe one.

steps.title: The word 'this' shows the sentence was sealed for this sin
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers from the פסוק 'they tested Me this ten times': the word 'this' teaches that the sentence was sealed for this particular sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: the פסוק says, 'They have tested Me this ten times.' The word 'this' teaches: for this sin the sentence was sealed.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש defends the משנה. He shows from a פסוק that the sentence was sealed specifically because of the spies' sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have said 'they tested Me ten times' without the word 'זה.' The extra word points to this sin, the spies' report, as the one that sealed the sentence. So it was not just the last drop; the פסוק names it as the cause.

keyTerms.meaning: They tested Me
This; here it points to the specific sin of the מרגלים
Ten times; the ten times the people tested God in the desert

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said: The verse says:
"They have tested Me this ten times,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 14:22. The key word is זה, "this."

phrases.english: for this, the sentence was sealed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading of a פסוק: an extra word shows the cause of the punishment.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the spies' sin was only the final sin that filled the measure.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'זה' shows the sentence was sealed because of this specific sin, so the משנה's proof stands.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's proof holds: the פסוק itself ties the sealed sentence to the spies' sin.

steps.title: A קל וחומר: bad talk about the land, and how much more about a person
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי אלעזר בן פרטא shows the power of לשון הרע from the מרגלים: if they were punished so much for speaking badly about wood and stones, someone who speaks badly about his friend is surely punished more.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי אלעזר בן פרטא said: Come and see how great the power of לשון הרע is. From where do we know? From the מרגלים. If one who spoke badly about wood and stones was punished like this, one who speaks badly about his friend, how much more so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that also learns the seriousness of לשון הרע from the מרגלים, using a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מרגלים only spoke badly about the land of ישראל, which is just wood and stones and has no feelings. Even so they were punished harshly. So speaking badly about a living person, who is really hurt, must be much worse.

keyTerms.meaning: Harmful, negative speech about others
One who spreads a bad name, slander
Wood and stones; here, the land of ישראל
How much more so; the ending of a קל וחומר

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן פַּרְטָא:
phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Elazar ben Perata says:

phrases.aramaic: בּוֹא וּרְאֵה כַּמָּה גָּדוֹל כֹּחַ שֶׁל לָשׁוֹן הָרָע,
phrases.english: Come and see how great the power of malicious speech is.
From where do we know? From the spies.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה הַמּוֹצִיא שֵׁם רַע עַל עֵצִים וַאֲבָנִים כָּךְ,
phrases.english: If one who spreads a bad name about wood and stones is punished like this,
phrases.notes: The wood and stones are the land of ישראל, which the spies spoke badly about.

phrases.english: one who spreads a bad name about his friend,
how much more so!

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן פַּרְטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the משנה's proof is defended, the גמרא brings a ברייתא that builds a similar lesson from the מרגלים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: לשון הרע is extremely severe: if slandering the land was punished so harshly, slandering a person is much worse.

steps.title: Maybe the spies were punished for speaking against God
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: maybe the spies were punished not for bad talk about the land, but for a terrible statement against God, as רבי חנינא בר פפא explains from 'ממנו.'
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know? Maybe it was because of what רבי חנינא בר פפא said. רבי חנינא בר פפא said: The spies said something terrible at that time, as it is written: 'For they are stronger than us.' Do not read it 'than us,' but 'than Him.' As if to say: even the Owner of the house cannot take His things out from there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the ברייתא's proof. It suggests the spies' punishment may have come from a much bigger sin, speaking against God's power.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ממנו' can mean 'than us' or 'than Him.' רבי חנינא בר פפא reads it as 'than Him,' meaning the spies said the Canaanites were too strong even for God, the Owner of the land. If that was their real sin, their punishment proves nothing about ordinary לשון הרע, and the קל וחומר breaks down.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not read it this way, but that way; a reading that adds a second meaning to a word
Can mean 'than us' or 'than Him'
As if it were possible to say; used when speaking about God in human terms
The owner of the house; here, God, the owner of the land
His utensils, his things; here, the people living in the land

phrases.aramaic: מִמַּאי? דִּלְמָא מִשּׁוּם דְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר פָּפָּא,
phrases.english: From where do we know? Perhaps it was because of what Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa said,
as Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa says:

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר גָּדוֹל דִּבְּרוּ מְרַגְּלִים בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה,
phrases.english: The spies said a terrible thing at that time,
as it is written: "For they are stronger than us,"

phrases.aramaic: אַל תִּיקְרֵי ״כִּי חָזָק הוּא מִמֶּנוּ״ אֶלָּא ״מִמֶּנּוּ״,
phrases.english: do not read "for they are stronger than us" but "than Him,"
phrases.notes: In Hebrew the same word ממנו can mean "than us" or "than Him," so he reads it the second way.

phrases.aramaic: כִּבְיָכוֹל, בַּעַל הַבַּיִת אֵין יָכוֹל לְהוֹצִיא כֵּלָיו מִשָּׁם.
phrases.english: as if to say, the Owner of the house cannot take His things out from there.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי? דִּלְמָא מִשּׁוּם דְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof used in the ברייתא of step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of the מרגלים to prove how severe לשון הרע is.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the spies were punished for speaking against God, their punishment does not show the power of לשון הרע, so the קל וחומר to slandering a friend does not work.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next move, where the גמרא must show that the punishment really was for the bad report itself.

steps.title: The spies died for their bad report about the land
steps.stepSummary: רבה, quoting ריש לקיש, proves from a פסוק that the מרגלים were punished for the bad report about the land, not only for speaking against God.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבה said in the name of ריש לקיש: the פסוק says 'And the men who brought out an evil report of the land died.' This means they died for the report about the land that they spread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 12. A פסוק shows the punishment came because of the bad report about the land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 suggested the spies were punished for a terrible statement against God, which would weaken the lesson of רבי אלעזר בן פרטא. The פסוק names them by their crime: 'those who brought out an evil report of the land.' So the punishment is tied to the bad talk about the land, and the קל וחומר about speaking badly of a friend still works.

keyTerms.meaning: The bad report about the land of ישראל
Those who spread a bad report
Rather; brings in a new answer

steps.whyThisMatters: This saves the ברייתא from step 11. The lesson that לשון הרע is very severe stays in place.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבָּה אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ,
phrases.english: Rather, Rabba said that Reish Lakish said:
The verse says:
"And the men died,
those who brought out an evil report of the land"
For the report of the land that they brought out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבָּה אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The spies were punished only for speaking against God, so the ברייתא proves nothing about לשון הרע
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק ties their death to the bad report about the land, so the ברייתא stands

steps.title: רבי יהודה lists the ten tests
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי יהודה lists the ten times our ancestors tested הקדוש ברוך הוא in the desert.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי יהודה says, our ancestors tested הקדוש ברוך הוא ten times: two at the sea, two with water, two with the מן, two with the quail, one with the golden calf, and one in the wilderness of פארן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives the list of the 'ten times' from the פסוק quoted in step 10. This sets up the explanation of each test that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 used the פסוק 'they tested Me this ten times.' Here רבי יהודה says what the ten were: 2+2+2+2+1+1. The last one, in מדבר פארן, is the story of the מרגלים, which is the main topic of the sugya.

keyTerms.meaning: A test; here, the people testing God's patience
The heavenly bread that fell in the desert
The quail God sent for meat
The golden calf
The wilderness of פארן, where the spies were sent from

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says,
Our ancestors made ten tests
of the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Two at the sea, and two with water,
phrases.notes: 'The sea' is the Sea of Reeds; 'water' means the times they complained about having no water to drink.

phrases.english: two with the manna, two with the quail,
one with the calf,
and one in the wilderness of Paran.
phrases.notes: This is the story of the spies, who were sent out from מדבר פארן.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, עֶשֶׂר נִסְיוֹנוֹת נִיסּוּ אֲבוֹתֵינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section listing the ten tests mentioned in the פסוק from step 10
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There were ten tests: two at the sea, two with water, two with the מן, two with the quail, one with the calf, and one in מדבר פארן.

steps.title: The first test at the sea: going down
steps.stepSummary: The two tests at the sea were one going in and one coming out. Going in, they complained: 'Were there no graves in Egypt?'
steps.simpleTranslation: Two at the sea: one going down into it, and one coming up out of it. Going down, as it is written: 'Is it because there are no graves in Egypt?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining the list, beginning with the two tests at the sea. It gives a פסוק for the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the sea split, the people were afraid and complained to משה that he brought them out to die. That complaint counts as the first test at the sea. The second test, coming out, is explained in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Going down into the sea
Coming up out of the sea
Graves

phrases.english: Two at the sea:
One going down and one coming up.
Going down, as it is written:
"Is it because there are no graves in Egypt?"

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנַיִם בַּיָּם: אַחַת בַּיְּרִידָה וְאַחַת בָּעֲלִיָּיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining the first item on רבי יהודה's list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first test at the sea was the complaint before going in: 'Were there no graves in Egypt?'

steps.title: The second test at the sea: little faith coming out
steps.stepSummary: The second test at the sea, coming out, follows רב הונא, who says that generation had little faith.
steps.simpleTranslation: Coming up, as רב הונא taught. For רב הונא said: the Jews of that generation were people of little faith.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second test at the sea with a teaching of רב הונא. It then sets up the next step, which shows where רב הונא gets this from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after seeing the sea split, the people still doubted. רב הונא calls them 'of little faith.' The גמרא does not stop here; it brings רבה בר מרי to show what that lack of faith looked like.

keyTerms.meaning: People of little faith
That generation (the one that left מצרים)

phrases.english: Coming up, as Rav Huna taught,
for Rav Huna said:
The Jews of that generation
were among those of little faith,

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֲלִיָּיה — כִּדְרַב הוּנָא, דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second test at the sea
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Coming out of the sea, the people showed little faith.

steps.title: They feared the Egyptians were coming up on the other side
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר מרי reads a פסוק in תהלים: the people rebelled at the sea by worrying that the Egyptians were coming out on the other side too.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבה בר מרי taught. For רבה בר מרי said: what is meant by 'They rebelled at the sea, at ים סוף, yet He saved them for His Name's sake'? It teaches that the Jews were rebellious then, saying: just as we are coming up on this side, the Egyptians are coming up on the other side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רב הונא with a פסוק explained by רבה בר מרי. It shows what the people's lack of faith was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says they 'rebelled at the sea,' which needs explaining, since God had just saved them. רבה בר מרי says the rebellion was doubt: they thought the Egyptians might also survive and come out on the far side. This doubt after a clear miracle is the second test at the sea.

keyTerms.meaning: Rebelling; acting against God
The Sea of Reeds that split
For the sake of His Name
It teaches; shows what we learn from the פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix the two tests. Going in, they were afraid of dying in the desert. Coming out, they doubted the miracle and thought the Egyptians were still alive.

phrases.english: as Rabba bar Mari taught,
for Rabba bar Mari said:
What is meant by what is written:
"But they rebelled at the sea, at the Sea of Reeds,
yet He saved them for His Name's sake"?

phrases.aramaic: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מַמְרִים בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה,
phrases.english: It teaches that the Jews were rebellious at that time,
and they were saying:
Just as we are coming up on this side,
so the Egyptians are coming up on the other side.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְרַבָּה בַּר מָרִי, דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר מָרִי: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source and details for רב הונא's statement in step 16
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's claim that the generation of the sea had little faith
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים 106:7-8, as explained by רבה בר מרי: they rebelled by fearing the Egyptians also came out of the sea

steps.title: God tells the sea to give back the Egyptians, and the sea objects
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא orders the שר של ים to spit the dead מצרים onto land. The sea complains that a gift should not be taken back, and הקדוש ברוך הוא promises one and a half times as many in the future.
steps.simpleTranslation: God said to the angel of the sea: 'Throw them out onto dry land!' The angel said: 'Master of the World, does a master give his servant a gift and then take it back?' God answered: 'I will give you one and a half times their number.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the story from the last step. To calm ישראל's fear that the מצרים escaped, הקדוש ברוך הוא tells the sea to show them the bodies on the shore.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dead מצרים were the sea's 'gift', food for its fish. The sea argues it is unfair to take a gift back. הקדוש ברוך הוא does not deny the claim and instead promises to repay it later with even more.

keyTerms.meaning: The angel in charge of the sea
Spit out, throw out
Dry land
A gift
One and a half (times as many)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְשַׂר שֶׁל יָם:
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to the angel of the sea:
Spit them out onto dry land!
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the drowned מצרים, so ישראל can see they are really dead.

phrases.english: He said before Him: Master of the World,
is there any servant
whose master gives him a gift
and then takes it back from him?
He said to him: I will give you
one and a half times their number.
phrases.notes: He means a future army, half again as big, that will drown in water.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְשַׂר שֶׁל יָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of the second test at the sea: it shows how ישראל's fear that the מצרים had come out was answered.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sea was ordered to give up the dead מצרים, and it was promised one and a half times as many in return.

steps.title: נחל קישון as guarantor, and the sea throws out the Egyptians
steps.stepSummary: The sea asks who will guarantee the promise. הקדוש ברוך הוא names נחל קישון as the guarantor, and the sea immediately throws the מצרים onto the shore, as the פסוק says.
steps.simpleTranslation: The angel said: 'Master of the World, can a servant sue his master?' God said: 'נחל קישון will be the guarantor.' Right away the sea threw them onto dry land, as it says: 'And ישראל saw מצרים dead upon the shore.'
steps.whatsHappening: The sea raises a second worry about getting paid back, and הקדוש ברוך הוא answers it. The story ends with a פסוק showing that ישראל saw the dead מצרים on the shore.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A servant cannot take his master to court, so the sea wants a guarantor (ערב). נחל קישון is named, the place where a later, bigger enemy army would be swept away. Once the promise was secured, the sea let go, and the פסוק proves ישראל saw the bodies.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes a legal claim, sues
The Kishon Brook
A guarantor who backs up a promise
It spat them out

steps.whatToRemember: The second test at the sea was ישראל's fear that the מצרים had escaped. הקדוש ברוך הוא answered it by having the sea throw the bodies onto the shore.

phrases.english: He said before Him: Master of the World,

phrases.aramaic: כְּלוּם יֵשׁ עֶבֶד שֶׁתּוֹבֵעַ אֶת רַבּוֹ?
phrases.english: is there a servant who can make a claim against his master?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: נַחַל קִישׁוֹן יִהְיֶה עָרֵב,
phrases.english: He said to him: The Kishon Brook will be a guarantor.
Immediately it spat them out onto dry land, as it is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״וַיַּרְא יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת מִצְרַיִם מֵת עַל וְגוֹ׳״
phrases.english: "And Israel saw Egypt dead upon etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּלוּם יֵשׁ עֶבֶד שֶׁתּוֹבֵעַ אֶת רַבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the dialogue with the sea's second objection and ends the story with a proof-פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With נחל קישון as guarantor, the sea threw the מצרים onto the land, and ישראל saw them dead.

steps.title: Two tests over water: the first at מרה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רבי יהודה's list of ten tests. Two were about water, at מרה and at רפידים. At מרה the water was bitter and the people complained against משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two tests were about water: at מרה and at רפידים. At מרה, as it says: 'They came to מרה and could not drink,' and it says: 'The people complained against משה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story of the sea is finished, so the גמרא goes back to the list of ten tests and explains the next two. It starts with מרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For each test the גמרא brings two פסוקים. One shows the problem (the water was undrinkable), and the other shows that the people complained instead of trusting הקדוש ברוך הוא.

keyTerms.meaning: Two tests involving water
Marah, a place where the water was bitter
Refidim, a place in the desert with no water
And they complained

phrases.english: Two with water —
phrases.notes: We're back to רבי יהודה's list of ten tests from step 14.

phrases.english: at Marah and at Refidim.
At Marah, as it is written:
"And they came to Marah and could not drink,"
And it is written: "And the people complained against Moshe."

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנַיִם בַּמַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the two tests at the sea, the גמרא returns to the list of ten tests and moves to the next pair.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first water test was at מרה, where the people complained about the bitter water.

steps.title: The second water test, at רפידים
steps.stepSummary: At רפידים there was no water, and the people fought with משה. Two פסוקים show this.
steps.simpleTranslation: At רפידים, as it says: 'They camped in רפידים and there was no water to drink,' and it says: 'The people fought with משה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the pair of water tests by showing the test at רפידים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It follows the same pattern as מרה: one פסוק shows the problem (no water at all), and one shows the people's reaction. Here it is stronger than complaining: they actually quarreled with משה.

keyTerms.meaning: And they camped
And they quarreled, fought

phrases.english: At Refidim, as it is written:
"And they camped in Refidim, and there was no water to drink,"
And it is written: "And the people fought with Moshe."

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּרְפִידִים דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the pair of water tests that the previous step began.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The second water test was at רפידים, where there was no water and the people fought with משה.

steps.title: Two tests involving the manna
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא names the next pair in רבי יהודה's list of ten tests, two that involved the מן, and starts to bring a פסוק as its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two of the tests were with the מן, as it is written:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next pair on the list, two tests involving the מן. This is a setup line, and the פסוקים that prove it come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא is following the same pattern it used for the water tests. First it names how many tests happened in one area, then it brings פסוקים to show each one. Here it has only said 'two with the מן' and opened with 'as it is written,' so the actual proof is still to come.

keyTerms.meaning: The manna, the food from heaven that fed בני ישראל in the desert
Two. Here it means two of the ten tests
As it is written. This introduces a פסוק as the source

phrases.english: Two with the manna, as it is written:

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנַיִם בַּמָּן דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of ten tests. It comes after the two water tests (steps 20 and 21) and moves to the next pair, the tests with the מן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two of the ten tests in the desert involved the מן, and the proof is about to be brought from פסוקים.
